newsitem.title: USA: Orbital satellite launch for NASA fails.
newsitem.headline: Orbital satellite launch for NASA fails.

text.p: A pair of NASA astronomy satellites launched by Orbital Sciences Corp failed to separate from a rocket after reaching orbit Monday, leaving scientists scrambling to salvage the mission, NASA officials said.
The satellites were launched by Virginia-based Orbital Sciences under a contract with National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

The two satellites, which are designed to study the sun and mysterious gamma ray bursts, were boosted into orbit by an air-launched Pegasus rocket but were not released from the third-stage of the rocket as planned.
The rocket was carried aloft by an L-1011 aircraft from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility and was launched over the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Virginia.
"It's quite disappointing to get this close and not finish the job the way we planned to do it," said J.R. Thompson, an official with Orbital Sciences.
